name: mbp-01-time-varying-environment
question:
Can v2ecoli's `media_update` / `exchange_data` Layer-1 Steps consume
an externally-driven, time-varying nutrient pool — instead of the
static media configuration baked into ParCa — such that metabolic
exchange fluxes and growth rate respond correctly to declining
glucose, declining DO, and other dynamic external concentrations?

variants.name: saturating-glucose-high
variants.note: far above PTS Km (Vmax ceiling check)

purpose.question:
Can v2ecoli's `media_update` / `exchange_data` Layer-1 Steps consume an
externally-driven, time-varying nutrient pool — instead of the static
media configuration baked into ParCa — such that metabolic exchange
fluxes and growth rate respond correctly to declining glucose, declining
DO, and other dynamic external concentrations?
purpose.mechanism:
v2ecoli's baseline composite currently treats the external environment as
a constant medium definition (constrained / unconstrained exchange sets
parameterized at composite-build time, see v2ecoli/steps/media_update.py
and metabolism's `exchange_data_from_media` method). For reactor
coupling, the external pool must be a TIME-VARYING store that external
physics writes into each timestep. This study introduces an
`EnvironmentDriver` Step (or a thin extension to `media_update`) that
reads from an `environment.external_concentrations` store (`map[float]`,
mM) and updates the constraints feeding metabolism each step. Reactor /
BiRD coupling (mbp-03) writes to that store; this study verifies the
plumbing in isolation by driving it with synthetic trajectories.
purpose.expected_outcome:
**mbp-01 is a PLUMBING study only** (per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3
+ investigation `discipline.scope_discipline`). It verifies that the
store→constraint wire works under extreme/saturating inputs that are
robust to v2ecoli's internal transport-kinetics functional form
(saturable MM / constant-bound / linear). Quantitative biological-
fidelity (gradient shape, μ response to glucose decline near Km,
acetate flux shift at sub-Vmax DO) is DEFERRED to a downstream
`transport-kinetics-fidelity` study — a candidate-future-study under
mbp-06 axis A.

Concretely under this study:
  - External-concentration changes propagate to metabolism's exchange
    constraint within one timestep (plumbing wire).
  - Cumulative mass balance closes (no leakage in the env-driver wire).
  - With external glucose held at 0, glucose exchange flux ≈ 0. Same
    for DO at zero. Universal biological floor; plumbing-confirming.
  - With external glucose at 5 g/L vs 50 g/L (both far above PTS Km),
    glucose uptake plateaus within ratio 0.9–1.1 (discriminates
    physical saturable/constant-bound implementations from unphysical
    linear scaling).
  - With external glucose at saturating 50 g/L, glucose uptake ≤
    published Vmax ceiling for E. coli glucose-PTS (~10–12 mmol/gDW/h).
  - Static-medium regression unchanged.

pipeline_gate.gate_status_summary:
First v2ecoli-enhancement study; no upstream dependencies. Gates the
reactor-coupling work — until the environment hook exists, BiRD's
dissolved O2 cannot drive v2ecoli's metabolism.

new_state_variables: environment.external_concentrations (map[float], mM) — populated by external physics each timestep
modified_processes: media_update / exchange_data: read external_concentrations (when env_driver_mode != static) instead of static media config. Backward-compatible default.
model_change.notes:
Internal v2ecoli enhancement — the smallest viable hook that lets
external physics drive v2ecoli's metabolism. Implementation must keep
the static-medium path untouched for existing baseline regressions
(verified by the static-env-regression sim above).

key_assumptions: v2ecoli's metabolism Process can re-read environment constraints every step (it already does via `exchange_data_from_media`).
External concentrations are well-mixed (single value per species across all agents in this single-cell study).
No timestep mismatch handled this phase — env updates and metabolism updates run on the same timebase.

behavior_tests.name: external_glucose_updates_propagate_within_one_step
behavior_tests.description: An external_glucose store update is reflected in metabolism's GLC[p] exchange constraint within one timestep. Direct wire check — replaces the removed `uptake-flux-tracks-external-glucose` Pearson test (which assumed linear response between concentration and uptake; v2ecoli's PTS is saturable).

behavior_tests.name: cumulative-mass-balance-closes
behavior_tests.description: Closed-balance cumulative mass conservation (MassConservationDeriver) — the relative cumulative residual between cell-mass change and net environmental exchange stays near zero, confirming the environment hook is wired without leakage.
behavior_tests.cites_note: No machine-linkable bib_key: the 0.0-0.05 band is a numerical mass-conservation closure tolerance (env-driver wire leakage check), not a literature-sourced biological value.

behavior_tests.name: static-env-baseline-unchanged
behavior_tests.description: With env_driver_mode=static, the composite produces the same baseline trajectory (e.g. DnaA count, growth rate) as the unmodified v2ecoli.composites.baseline. Regression guard.

behavior_tests.name: zero-substrate-blocks-uptake
behavior_tests.description: external_glucose held at 0 → glucose exchange flux ≈ 0 (numerical tolerance). Same for DO: zero external DO → O2 exchange flux ≈ 0. Universal biological floor; also confirms plumbing.

behavior_tests.name: saturating-substrate-respects-vmax
behavior_tests.description: external_glucose held at 50 g/L (~30,000× PTS Km) → glucose exchange flux ≤ published Vmax for E. coli glucose-PTS (~10–12 mmol/gDW/h). Catches the unphysical linear-scaling implementation case.

behavior_tests.name: plateau-across-saturating-range
behavior_tests.description: Two runs at 5 g/L and 50 g/L (both far above PTS Km) → GUR within a tight ratio tolerance. Both above Km, so saturable and constant-bound models predict matching GUR; linear scaling would predict ~10× difference. Direct discriminator between physical and unphysical implementations.

open_questions.question:
Is per-timestep external_concentrations update fast enough, or does
metabolism need a longer "constant medium" window (e.g. 1 min) to
avoid solver-instability artifacts in v2ecoli's FBA inner solve?

Should env_driver_mode default to `static` (preserves existing
baseline behavior, opt-in to time-varying) or `external_store`
(opt-out)? Preference is `static` for backward compatibility but
confirm with v2ecoli baseline maintainer.

Should claims carry a `functional_form` field (saturable / step /
linear / threshold) so tests can pick the right measure shape and
lint-time validation can flag mismatched bindings? Raised in
chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §2 as a pbg-superpowers schema extension.
Tracked as an upstream PR candidate via mbp-06 axis-E.

Surfaced 2026-05-28 while implementing the media_update consumption
path: baseline_time_varying_env adds `state["environment"]` at the
TOP LEVEL of the composite, but MediaUpdate (and ExchangeData) live
inside `agents.0` and resolve their topology port `("environment",)`
to `state["agents"]["0"]["environment"]` — a DIFFERENT store. The
two are never wired together, so EnvironmentDriver writes to the
top-level store and MediaUpdate sees nothing. Three resolution
options (none yet picked):

  (a) Make EnvironmentDriver per-agent — every cell gets its own
      driver. Loses the "one driver feeds the population" semantic
      that mbp-02 + mbp-03 rely on (reactor coupler is one source
      of truth feeding all cells); reject unless we add a separate
      coordination mechanism on top.

  (b) Widen MediaUpdate's class-level topology to read top-level
      environment via an absolute path (or `("..", "..",
      "environment")` upward traversal). Smallest code change but
      touches every architecture (baseline, departitioned,
      reconciled) — regression risk on the baseline composite that
      has no top-level environment store. Would need careful
      conditional topology.

  (c) Add a small tick-leading mirror Step inside
      baseline_time_varying_env that, each tick, copies
      `state["environment"]["external_concentrations"]` into each
      `state["agents"][i]["environment"]["external_concentrations"]`.
      Most additive — no class-level changes; localized to this one
      composite. Doubles as the natural place to resolve the
      molecule-ID convention gap below (see
      `env-driver-molecule-id-convention`). RECOMMENDED.

Resolution gates the 5 mbp-01 plumbing/extreme tests
(test_external_glucose_updates_propagate_within_one_step,
test_cumulative_mass_balance_closes, test_zero_substrate_blocks_uptake,
test_saturating_substrate_respects_vmax,
test_plateau_across_saturating_range).
open_questions.resolution:
Adopted option (c) — added EnvironmentMirror Step that runs each tick
BEFORE the FLUSH barrier preceding `media_update`'s layer. The mirror
reads top-level state['environment']['external_concentrations'] and
writes the driver-derived delta DIRECTLY to each agent's
boundary.external (which has a typed schema; bypasses the
per-agent environment store the original gap was about). PBG's FLUSH
commits the mirror's writes before exchange_data reads boundary —
propagation completes same-tick. Landed in commit 60cdbd3; all 5
previously-blocked tests now pass alongside the static-mode
regression (full sim suite: 32 passed, 15 skipped).

open_questions.question:
Surfaced 2026-05-28 alongside `env-store-topology-mismatch`: the
EnvironmentDriver emits compartment-tagged molecule IDs (e.g.
"GLC[p]" per the synthetic_trajectory_spec convention used in
mbp-01 sims), but `boundary.external` (the store ExchangeData
reads) uses BARE names — "GLC", "ACET", "FUM", "MAL", "SUC", ...
across all 87 entries, no compartment suffix. So even if the
topology gap above is closed, MediaUpdate would look up
`boundary_ext.get("GLC[p]")`, miss, and skip silently.

Three resolution options (none yet picked):

  (a) Have the driver use bare names. Cleanest if the convention
      isn't load-bearing elsewhere — needs audit of where else
      compartment-tagged IDs are used (e.g. emit paths, parquet
      hive schemas).

  (b) Have MediaUpdate strip the compartment suffix at read time.
      Hides the convention difference inside the consumer; cheap
      but every other consumer would need the same logic.

  (c) Have the mirror Step (see `env-store-topology-mismatch`
      option c) do both the copy AND the ID normalization in one
      place. Pairs cleanly with the recommended topology fix.
      RECOMMENDED.

Resolution gates the same 5 tests as the topology question above
— both gaps must close before mbp-01's plumbing/extreme suite can
run.
open_questions.resolution:
Bare-name convention adopted — driver synthetic_trajectory_spec keys
match boundary.external keys directly ('GLC', 'ACET', ...). The
EnvironmentMirror Step (closes env-store-topology-mismatch above)
looks up `boundary.external[mol]` per driver-supplied key; any
unmatched name (e.g. compartment-tagged 'GLC[p]') is silently
skipped — fails closed without crashing. Bundled with the
topology fix in the same commit.

Debug listener on metabolism.exchange_data_from_media's output set; verify it updates each step

candidate_causes: EnvironmentDriver runs even with env_driver_mode=static and overwrites the constant medium
Composite-build wiring changes Layer-1 Step ordering
checks: Diff per-cell observables vs an unmodified baseline run at seed 0 — should be byte-identical
Verify EnvironmentDriver short-circuits in static mode

candidate_causes: EnvironmentDriver writes concentrations in different units than metabolism reads (mM vs mmol/L vs g/L)
Per-cell uptake flux not multiplied by cell mass to get total mmol uptaken
Volume not held constant in the batch run

Verify the integrand: total_uptake = sum_t(flux × cell_mass × dt)

limitations: PLUMBING-ONLY scope (per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3). Gradient-shape and quantitative-biological-fidelity tests (e.g. μ response to glucose decline near Km, acetate flux shift at sub-Vmax DO, GUR-vs-[glucose] curve) are deferred to a `transport-kinetics-fidelity` candidate-future-study under mbp-06 axis A.

REMOVED tests with rationale (kept here so future agents don't re-add them by reflex): `uptake-flux-tracks-external-glucose` (Pearson ≥ 0.7 assumed linear response; real PTS is saturable, ~3 orders of magnitude above the sweep range — test fails on every realistic implementation). `low-do-clamp-reduces-o2-uptake` (5 µM DO clamp is 25-200× above cytochrome bd/bo3 Km, so OUR shouldn't reduce at this clamp; Vemuri 2006 supports acetate-RISE under low DO, not OUR-drop — citation/test mismatch). `mu-drops-when-glucose-depletes` (kinetics-dependent; defer to transport-kinetics-fidelity study).
Single cell only; population aggregation is mbp-02's job.
Reactor physics (kLa, gas transport) not coupled here — that is mbp-03.
Time-varying-medium support assumes the same exchange-molecule set as static medium; new species require ParCa regeneration.

implementation_requirements.title: EnvironmentDriver Step
implementation_requirements.description:
PBG Step that, each timestep, writes to environment.external_concentrations
from either (a) an external source store (default for reactor coupling),
or (b) a synthetic trajectory function (for unit testing this phase).
Hooks the existing media_update to read from this store when
env_driver_mode != static.

implementation_requirements.description:
Thin wrapper around v2ecoli.composites.baseline that injects
EnvironmentDriver and the environment.external_concentrations store.
Backward-compatible default: env_driver_mode=static.

report.headline: Verify v2ecoli can consume an externally-driven, time-varying nutrient pool (plumbing only) so reactor physics can later drive metabolism.
report.summary: The EnvironmentDriver + EnvironmentMirror wire (commit 60cdbd3) propagates external-concentration updates to metabolism within one tick. The env-store topology and molecule-ID-convention gaps were RESOLVED via a tick-leading mirror Step writing to boundary.external. The study's own resolution note records all 5 plumbing/extreme tests passing alongside the static-mode regression (32 passed / 15 skipped). Quantitative transport-kinetics fidelity is explicitly DEFERRED to a downstream transport-kinetics-fidelity study (mbp-06 axis A).

study_card.one_liner: Plumbing study: store->constraint wire for a time-varying external environment.
study_card.deliverable: EnvironmentDriver Step + baseline_time_varying_env composite + 5 plumbing/extreme tests + static-mode regression.

enforced_params.name: env_driver_mode
enforced_params.note: static path kept byte-identical for regression

biological_summary: PLUMBING-ONLY (per chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3): verifies the wire under extreme/saturating inputs robust to v2ecoli's internal transport-kinetics functional form (saturable MM / constant-bound / linear). Biological floors checked: zero external substrate -> zero exchange flux; uptake at 50 g/L respects the published E. coli glucose-PTS Vmax (~10-12 mmol/gDW/h); uptake plateaus across 5 vs 50 g/L (saturable kinetics). Gradient-shape / mu-vs-[glucose] fidelity is deferred.

literature_anchors.note: Monod 1949 anchors the saturable-kinetics plateau premise (plateau-across-saturating-range). Other test bands are numerical-tolerance / model-internal / plumbing-spec (see per-test cites_note) and have no machine-linkable source.

design_pivot_required.note: PIVOTED to plumbing-only (chris_feedback_2026_05_26 §3): removed 3 transport-kinetics tests (uptake-flux-tracks-external-glucose Pearson, low-do-clamp-reduces-o2-uptake, mu-drops-when-glucose-depletes) that assumed a functional form v2ecoli does not commit to; fidelity deferred to transport-kinetics-fidelity (mbp-06 axis A). See limitations.

conclusion_verdicts.statement: Env-driver plumbing wire verified: external-concentration updates reach metabolism within one tick after the EnvironmentMirror fix (60cdbd3); the study's resolution note records all 5 plumbing/extreme tests + static-mode regression passing (32 passed / 15 skipped).
conclusion_verdicts.evidence: open_questions env-store-topology-mismatch + env-driver-molecule-id-convention (status: resolved); runs[] (3 parquet runs); charts 00 (static regression) + 01 (driven-env propagation).

conclusion_verdicts.statement: Quantitative transport-kinetics fidelity (GUR-vs-[glucose] shape, mu response near Km, acetate at sub-Vmax DO) is out of scope.
conclusion_verdicts.evidence: limitations[0]; routed to mbp-06 axis A transport-kinetics-fidelity candidate-future-study.
